site.name: Atelier Lucius Vennius
site.concept: The working portfolio of Lucius Vennius, a contemporary architect and mosaicist whose practice draws directly from the building grammar of Imperial Rome.

card_pattern: Each project module is a rectangular travertine-cream card with a thin ink-black Greek-key border tiled along its top and bottom edges. The project title sits inside a small laurel roundel at the top-center of the card, set in tracked Marcellus capitals. A 3:2 image plate sits centered below the title, followed by a short Inter body block (location, year, client, materials) flush to a single column. A vine-leaf ornament in pompeian red separates the metadata strip from the descriptive paragraph.
design_rules: Travertine cream dominates the page; pompeian red and gold leaf appear only as small accents on rules, ornaments, and emphasis. Every hero, title, and section seal is centered on a strict vertical axis, framed by either a pediment outline or a wreath roundel. Headings are Roman square capitals tracked tight; body sets in generous golden-ratio columns with 1.65 line-height.

pages.title: Atelier Lucius Vennius — Architecture & Mosaic
pages.content_brief: Centered hero framed by a pediment with the studio name in Marcellus capitals and a one-line tagline: 'Building in the grammar of Rome — Genoa, MMXXIV.' Below, a three-column synopsis introducing the practice (architecture, mosaic restoration, civic monuments), each headed by an oak-wreath roundel. Closes with a short manifesto paragraph quoting Vitruvius on firmitas, utilitas, venustas.

pages.title: Selected Works — Atelier Lucius Vennius
pages.content_brief: A grid of six built and unbuilt projects, each with a project number (I–VI), a Latin title, and a short caption. Examples: 'I. Thermae Liguriae — public baths, Sestri Levante, 2022'; 'II. Domus Vennia — private residence, Tivoli, 2021'; 'III. Mosaic of the Four Seasons — restoration, Villa di Casale, 2020'. Each card carries a Greek-key border and an image plate.

pages.title: Mosaic Studio — Atelier Lucius Vennius
pages.content_brief: Dedicated page for the mosaic restoration practice. Opens with a centered laurel-framed title 'OPUS TESSELLATUM'. Body covers tessera sourcing (Carrara, Verona rosso, Egyptian porphyry), conservation method, and three case studies: the Orpheus pavement at Volubilis (consultancy, 2019), the Casa del Fauno border reconstruction (2021), and a contemporary commission for the Banca di Liguria atrium (2023).

pages.title: Studio & Method — Atelier Lucius Vennius
pages.content_brief: Biographical and methodological page. Lucius Vennius, b. Ravenna 1978, trained at the Politecnico di Milano and the Scuola di Restauro di Spoleto. Practice founded 2011. Describes the studio's working method: hand-drawn axial plans, full-scale cartoons for mosaic, scale plaster models for vaults. Includes a list of collaborators (structural engineer Marco Fenoglio, master mason Giulia Trevi).

pages.title: Writing & Lectures — Atelier Lucius Vennius
pages.content_brief: Chronological list of published essays and lectures. Sample entries: 'On the Coffer as Structural Honesty,' Domus, March 2023; 'The Pediment Returns,' lecture at the British School at Rome, October 2022; 'Mosaic and the Patient Hand,' Casabella, December 2021. Each entry has a short two-sentence abstract underneath.

pages.title: Studio Visit & Correspondence — Atelier Lucius Vennius
pages.content_brief: Centered contact card framed by a laurel wreath. Studio address: Via dei Coronari 47, 00186 Roma. Visiting hours by appointment, Tuesday through Friday, 10:00–17:00. Telephone +39 06 4521 9970. Correspondence: studio@vennius.atelier. Brief paragraph welcoming inquiries for new commissions, restoration consultancies, and academic collaborations.
